# Synthetic teaching note: allometric scaling of clearance and volume

This note is a synthetic fixture written for the PharmAgent test suite. It is not
taken from any book or paper.

## 1 Fixed exponents

Allometric scaling relates a pharmacokinetic parameter to body size through a
power function of weight normalised to a reference of seventy kilograms. The
theory-based exponents are 0.75 for clearance and 1.0 for volume of distribution.
Many analysts fix these exponents rather than estimate them, because a sparse
adult dataset rarely contains enough weight range to identify the exponent with
useful precision.

## 2 Estimated exponents

When the weight range is wide, for example in a paediatric population, the
exponent on clearance may be estimated. An estimated exponent far from 0.75 that
is also imprecise is a warning sign rather than a discovery. Maturation of
clearance in neonates and infants is better handled by an explicit maturation
function of postmenstrual age than by letting the allometric exponent absorb it.

## 3 Covariate confounding

Weight is correlated with age, body surface area and organ function. Including
weight by allometry first and then testing other covariates on the residual
variability avoids attributing a size effect to an unrelated covariate.

## 4 Reporting

State whether exponents were fixed or estimated, give the reference weight, and
report the typical value at the reference weight so results can be compared across
studies.
